column1: # ================ *** WHAT THIS SETTLES AND WHAT IT OPENS *** ================
# *** IT STRENGTHENS THE BAPTISM NULL RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. *** The obvious worry - that the family
# used a different Rosario parish and the Catedral books would never show them - *** does not hold for
# 1882. *** Four of the five parishes have no register that early; the earliest is Santa Rosa de Lima in
# 1888. In February 1882 the Catedral was, so far as the filmed record goes, the only parish in Rosario.
# So reading its index end to end for 1731-1901 was the right thing to have done, and the answer stands.
# *** BUT IT OPENS A REAL NEW SOURCE ON THE CENTRAL QUESTION. *** SANTA ROSA DE LIMA, Confirmaciones
# 1890-1897, *** DGS 004581639, 141 images, transcribed in FULL TEXT. *** Its own index page reads:
#     "Confirmacion administrada por el Senor Obispo DOCTOR DON JUAN CAGLIERO en el mes de Julio de
#      1890 en la Iglesia Parroquial de Santa Rosa" - with further rounds in SEPTIEMBRE y OCTUBRE 1891
#      and MAYO 1897.
# *** Pablo Armando was EIGHT in July 1890, NINE in 1891 and FIFTEEN in 1897. *** The confirmations read
# this morning at the Catedral cover the same years from the other parish. If he was confirmed at
# Rosario at all, he is in one book or the other.
# *** AND THE FILM WARNS OF ITS OWN DAMAGE: *** the index page carries the words "PAGES MISSING".
# Whatever this register does not contain, it may be because the leaves are gone rather than because
# the name is absent. That must be said with any null taken from it.
# ---- HOW THE DGS WAS FOUND, because the ordinary route failed ----
# The FamilySearch CATALOGUE SEARCH was down again ("Something Went Wrong"), so the film number could
# not be looked up. It was recovered instead from the image viewer's own page source, where the waypoint
# payload carries it. *** Browse by waypoint -> read the DGS out of the page -> then use the ordinary
# /search/film/<DGS>?i=N loop. *** Worth writing down: it works when the catalogue does not.
